permutationLabel: Elderly (79) septic shock — multiple small cholangitic abscesses from an occluded biliary stent
summary: 79-year-old man with a plastic biliary stent overdue for exchange: confusion, fever 39.4 °C, BP 84/48 on noradrenaline, lactate 4.6, creatinine 190, platelets 88; CT: multiple ≤2 cm abscesses in the right lobe, dilated ducts with an occluded stent.

inputs.hpi: ERCP with a plastic stent 5 months ago for bile duct stones; stent exchange was due at 3 months but missed. Two days of fevers and rigors, now drowsy and confused. Oliguric today.

exam.general: Drowsy, confused (GCS 13). Temperature 39.4°C, pulse 124/min, BP 84/48 despite 30 mL/kg crystalloid; noradrenaline started. Mildly jaundiced. Septic shock.

imaging.name: CT abdomen (contrast)
imaging.result: Multiple small (≤2 cm) rim-enhancing abscesses clustered in the right lobe. Intrahepatic duct dilatation with an occluded plastic CBD stent and residual duct stones. Pneumobilia absent.

surgicalHistory: ERCP, sphincterotomy and plastic biliary stent (5 months ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Multiple pyogenic (cholangitic) liver abscesses with septic shock
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Multiple cholangitic pyogenic liver abscesses with septic shock (noradrenaline, confusion, AKI, thrombocytopenia) from an occluded plastic biliary stent with retained duct stones.

emergencyLevel.note: iOS (predicted, not observed): routine — "Fever and confusion" contains no emergency or urgent keyword.

mustInclude.note: Critical-care admission for septic shock now — an "ICU post-operatively" line attached to a laparotomy consent does not count.
Multiple small cholangitic abscesses are treated by draining the obstructed biliary tree (stent exchange), not by percutaneous drainage of each abscess.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: Hepatic abscess: diagnosis and management (narrative review — no formal international guideline exists)
guideline.section: Pyogenic abscess: blood cultures, CT, antibiotics for 4–6 weeks, percutaneous drainage/aspiration for larger abscesses, look for a biliary or colonic source; multiple cholangitic abscesses: treat the biliary obstruction
guideline.citation: Lardière-Deguelte S, Ragot E, Amroun K, et al. J Visc Surg. 2015;152:231–243.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholangitis
guideline.section: Grade II: any two of WBC >12,000 or <4,000/mm³, fever ≥39 °C, age ≥75, total bilirubin ≥5 mg/dL, hypoalbuminaemia (<0.7 × LLN); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Kiriyama S, Kozaka K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:17–30.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for acute cholangitis
guideline.section: Grade II: early biliary drainage; Grade III: organ support then urgent biliary drainage
guideline.citation: Miura F, Okamoto K, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:31–40.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines 2021
guideline.section: Blood cultures before antimicrobials; antimicrobials within 1 h for shock; source control; noradrenaline first-line vasopressor
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: elderly patient in septic shock with a biliary source. Source control is urgent biliary drainage (stent exchange) with organ support and antibiotics; tests shock recognition and the biliary-source branch.

authoring.author: Claude (HPB cluster)
